title: 五十万の融通  (Five Hundred Thousand Yen)

segments.t: In episode two of The Naked Director, Toru Muranishi and Toshi scramble to raise startup cash in Sapporo. Inside a small loan office, Muranishi puts up the deed to his house and stamps his personal seal before stepping outside to compare totals with Toshi. Let's hear the Japanese dialogue first without worrying about catching every word.
はい、自宅の権利書です。
うちで五十万融通しますよ。
どうも。
利子は十日で一割です。
いろいろ契約のことが書いてあります。
構いません。はい、実印です。
じゃ、押させてもらいますよ。
よろしくお願いします。
おい、どうだった？
五十万だ。
俺は全部で百万だな。
もういいんじゃないか？
Muranishi stays brisk and polite inside the loan office, then switches to plain talk outside with Toshi. Let's walk through the key lines.
はい、自宅の権利書です。

'Here is the deed to my house.' "Jitaku" means one's own home, a slightly more formal cousin of "ie", house. Linking it with "no" to "kenrisho", title deed, names the document without needing a separate word for 'my'.
うちで五十万融通しますよ。

'Our shop can lend you five hundred thousand yen.' "Uchi" literally means home or inside, and businesspeople use it warmly for 'our shop' or 'our company'. "Gojuuman" counts fifty units of "man", ten thousand.
どうも。
'Thanks.' A quick "doumo" works like an all-purpose nod that can mean thanks, hello, or excuse me depending on the moment.
利子は十日で一割です。
'Interest is ten percent every ten days.' "Tooka" is the special ten-day counter, while "ichiwari" means one tenth—ten percent—using Japanese's everyday "wari" system for tenths.
構いません。
'I do not mind.' "Kamaimasen" is the polite negative of "kamau", to care or mind, handy whenever you want to say 'that's fine with me'.
はい、実印です。
'Here is my registered seal.' In Japan, major contracts are stamped with a "jitsuin", a personal seal officially registered at city hall rather than signed by pen.
よろしくお願いします。
'Thank you for taking care of this.' "Yoroshiku onegai shimasu" seals a deal or favor ahead of time, asking the other person to treat the matter kindly.
おい、どうだった？
'Hey, how did it go?' "Dou datta" pairs "dou", how, with plain past "datta", was—the natural casual way to ask a friend how something went.
俺は全部で百万だな。
'I got one million in total.' Toshi calls himself "ore", a rough masculine 'I', and sums things up with "zenbu de", in all. "Hyakuman" is one hundred ten-thousands: one million.
もういいんじゃないか？

'Is that not enough now?' "Mou ii" alone can mean 'already good' or 'enough already', and softened with "n ja nai ka" it nudges Muranishi to agree. Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
はい、自宅の権利書です。
うちで五十万融通しますよ。
どうも。
利子は十日で一割です。
いろいろ契約のことが書いてあります。
構いません。はい、実印です。
じゃ、押させてもらいますよ。
よろしくお願いします。
おい、どうだった？
五十万だ。
俺は全部で百万だな。
もういいんじゃないか？
Notice how Japanese counts big sums in units of "man", ten thousand, so fifty ten-thousands gives five hundred thousand and a hundred ten-thousands makes a million. Until next time, take care.
じゃあね。

source.show: 全裸監督 (The Naked Director) S01E02
